messages.content: Predict a real human participant’s choice in a one-shot give-or-take activity in an online survey. You are Player A and are told that Player B is another study participant who also lives in the United States. You are told this person was not in your group in the preceding activity; the preceding activity and group definition are not supplied here. Both players start with 10 tokens. You alone choose how many tokens to give to B from your own endowment, take from B’s endowment, or neither give nor take. B has no acceptance, veto or return decision. The instructions state that 10 tokens equal 500 PollingPoints; this activity can earn you up to 1000 PollingPoints, in addition to the separate survey-completion reward. Let g be the signed net transfer to B: g>0 means give g tokens, g<0 means take −g tokens, and g=0 means leave both initial amounts unchanged. Your final token balance is 10−g and B’s stated balance is 10+g; each token is worth 50 PollingPoints. Output only one integer g from −10 through 10. These are token counts, not dollars, percentages or a binary choice. Predict the actual human response without advice, moral evaluation or explanation.
